subject: Autoscale assumptions & checklist — follow up from discovery call
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@checkoutly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Autoscale assumptions & checklist — follow up from discovery call

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can validate capacity and SLOs for Checkoutly:

Summary of what you described
- Target P95 latency: 250ms for synchronous generation (prompt sizes up to ~512 tokens).
- Streaming requirement: first partial token must start streaming within 100ms of request acceptance for live checkout experiences.
- Expected steady-state concurrency: 200 concurrent interactive sessions; peak burst traffic up to ~2,200 QPS during promotional events (approx. 3–5 minute peaks).
- Tolerance for queueing/backpressure: acceptable up to 10s for non-critical batch jobs, but interactive checkout flows need sub-1s tail.
- Warm pool expectation: you asked for instance warm pools to reduce scale-up time; target: <45s to meet p95 SLO during a burst.

Concrete asks / next steps for your team (can you provide by EOD Wed?)
1) Traffic profile: sample CSV of 24h request timestamps + token counts (we'll use this to simulate bursts).
2) Percent distribution of prompt lengths (0–64, 65–256, 257–512, >512).
3) Which endpoints require streaming vs. non-streaming.
4) Priority tiers: which traffic must never be queued (billing/checkout) vs. best-effort (background personalization).

What we'll deliver after we get those artifacts
- Run a targeted throughput and concurrency simulation against our dedicated pools to validate whether p95=250ms and streaming start <=100ms can be met with your peak patterns.
- A short checklist (attached) showing warm-pool sizing options, expected scale-up curves, and recommended queueing policies.
- Suggested canary plan for a staged rollout during your next promo window.

I've attached the assumptions/checklist workbook and a template for the traffic sample. Ben and Naomi are on copy — Ben will own the simulation plan; Naomi will help size warm pools and streaming verification.

If anything above is incorrect, call it out and I'll update. Otherwise, Samir/Priya — can you share the sample CSV and prompt distribution by Wed 21 Jul?

Best,

Marissa Cole
Strategic Sales (West) | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: autoscale-assumptions-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet, 3 tabs: assumptions, warm-pool-options, canary-plan)

Subject: Re: Autoscale assumptions & checklist — follow up from discovery call

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few clarifications:
- The 250ms p95 is for single-shot recommendations during checkout (no streaming). Streaming is only for the live upsell widget and must hit the 100ms start requirement.
- Peak bursts: typically last ~4 minutes, with the 2,200 QPS number being 99th-percentile minute during Black Friday-like promos.
- Priority: checkout_authorize and payment_flow are gold (no queueing). personalization_feed and cross-sell-batch are bronze.

We'll pull together the CSV and distribution and aim to send by Wed 21 Jul. A couple of questions to help prioritize:
1) For warm pools, are you recommending pinned warm instances for gold endpoints only, or a shared warm pool across endpoints?
2) If our peak is 2,200 QPS, roughly how many GPUs or shards should we expect might be needed? We understand you’ll simulate but a rough order of magnitude helps internal approval.

I'll upload the sample traffic to the Drive link you shared once it's ready.

Thanks,
Samir
VP Product | Checkoutly
samir@checkoutly.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Autoscale assumptions & checklist — follow up from discovery call

Hi Samir / Priya —

Quick technical notes to help with your two questions. I'll summarize expectations and what we'll validate in the run: 

Warm-pool strategy (recommendation)
- Hybrid: pin a small dedicated warm pool for gold endpoints (checkout_authorize, payment_flow) sized to cover typical burst baseline (~25% of expected peak) and use shared warm instances for the rest. This reduces cold-start exposure for mission-critical flows while saving cost.
- Warm pool warmup: we define "warmed" as model weights + KV cache primed for your top-100 prompt prefixes. Time-to-warmed depends on model size/quantization; typical: 18–40s on our optimized runtime if the instance has preloaded weights. Cold boot (no warm pool) to fully ready can be 85–140s depending on GPU type.

Capacity ballpark for 2,200 QPS (order of magnitude)
- If using a 13B-class model (mixed-precision, int8-like execution), one xG-optimized GPU can sustain approx 80–120 RPS for interactive requests at median prompt lengths; for p95 targets you should assume lower per-GPU throughput.
- Ballpark: 20–40 GPUs to handle steady 2,200 RPS with target latency headroom. Exact number depends on prompt length mix and whether streaming adds extra token-level CPU work. We'll refine after running your CSV through our simulator.

Queueing/backpressure behavior
- By default we favor graceful degradation: priority traffic is routed to warm/pinned pools; overflow is queued with a short timeout (configurable). For gold flows we'll recommend immediate preemption and dedicated capacity; for bronze flows we can expose a 10s retry window and eventual 429s after policy.

What we'll validate in the simulation
- p95 latency under your actual prompt-length distribution and observed burst shapes.
- Streaming-start delta (time from req accept -> first token) under warm vs cold instances.
- Scale-up curves: time from detection of 0->X additional capacity to effective throughput increase. We'll show both autoscale and warm-pool-only scenarios.

Action: once we get the CSV and distribution we'll run a targeted sim and share a 1-page ops recommendation + a slide showing estimated GPU counts for three model-size options (7B / 13B / 70B) within 3 business days.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: current-traffic-sample.csv (template filled with anonymized timestamps and token counts)
